label: TP-Link TL-SG1005P
description: TP-Link TL-SG1005P - five-port unmanaged gigabit desktop switch with PoE+ on four ports: 5x 10/100/1000 RJ45, 802.3af/at on ports 1-4 at up to 30 W each against a 65 W total budget, port 5 plain copper, 10 Gbps switching capacity, fanless, external 53.5 V DC adapter.

poe.note: PoE standard 802.3af/at, ports 1-4, up to 30 W per port, 65 W PoE power budget. Intelligent power management cuts lower-priority ports when total draw exceeds 65 W, so four 30 W devices cannot all be powered: the budget, not the port count, is the limit. PoE auto recovery on ports 1-4; extend mode on ports 1-2 only, where the port rate drops to 10 Mbps for runs up to 250 m - extend mode is a port setting, not modelled as a separate interface.

fabric.note: Vendor switching capacity of 10 Gbps, the full-duplex aggregate of the five gigabit ports (5 Gbps each way).

notes: TP-Link figures for the current revision, datasheet TL-SG1005P(UN) 6.0 (https://static.tp-link.com/upload/product-overview/2026/202609/20260924/TL-SG1005P(UN)6.0_datasheet.pdf), checked against the product pages at https://www.tp-link.com/us/business-networking/unmanaged-switch/tl-sg1005p/v2/ and https://www.tp-link.com/uk/business-networking/unmanaged-switch/tl-sg1005p/v2/. Hardware: 5x 10/100/1000 Mbps RJ45, auto negotiation and auto MDI/MDIX, PoE+ ports 1-4 at up to 30 W each with a 65 W budget, 2 K MAC table, 1 Mbit packet buffer, 9 KB jumbo frames (the product pages quote 16 KB while the datasheet quotes 9 KB - the datasheet is used here), 7.44 Mpps forwarding, store-and-forward, IEEE 802.3x flow control, 802.1p/DSCP QoS, IGMP snooping, fanless metal desktop/wall case 99.8 x 98 x 25 mm fed by an external 53.5 V DC / 1.31 A adapter, 74.54 W maximum consumption with a 65 W load, MTBF 578,246 h at 25 C, operating range -5 to 40 C. REVISION NOTE: V1 of this model is NOT the same box - the V1 datasheet lists 802.3af only, 15.4 W per PoE port and a 56 W budget (https://www.tp-link.com/us/business-networking/unmanaged-switch/tl-sg1005p/v1/). This entry follows the current V2/V6 datasheet, so it can power a 30 W 802.3at device that a V1 chassis could not; a lab built from a V1 unit is the one case where this entry overstates the hardware.

label: TP-Link TL-SG1008P
description: TP-Link TL-SG1008P - eight-port unmanaged gigabit desktop switch with PoE+ on four ports: 8x 10/100/1000 RJ45, 802.3af/at on ports 1-4 at up to 30 W each against a 64 W total budget, 16 Gbps switching capacity, fanless, external 54 V DC adapter.

poe.note: PoE standard 802.3af/at, PoE+ ports 1-4 only, up to 30 W per port, 64 W budget for all four. Intelligent power management sheds the lowest-priority port once draw passes 64 W. Ports 5-8 carry data only, so eight powered devices on this box is a cabling error the spec should refuse.

fabric.note: Vendor switching capacity of 16 Gbps, the full-duplex aggregate of the eight gigabit ports (8 Gbps each way).

notes: TP-Link figures from the current product page (https://www.tp-link.com/us/business-networking/unmanaged-switch/tl-sg1008p/), with the PoE split cross-checked on the UK page (https://www.tp-link.com/uk/business-networking/unmanaged-switch/tl-sg1008p/). Hardware: 8x 10/100/1000 Mbps RJ45, auto negotiation and auto MDI/MDIX, PoE+ on ports 1-4 at up to 30 W each against a 64 W budget, 16 Gbps switching capacity, 11.904 Mpps forwarding, 4 K MAC table, 16 KB jumbo frames, store-and-forward, 802.1p/DSCP QoS, IGMP snooping, fanless metal case 171 x 98 x 27 mm with a physical security lock and an external 54 V DC / 1.3 A adapter, 5.4 W idle and 75 W with the full 64 W PoE load, operating range 0 to 40 C. Unmanaged: plug and play, no CLI, no HTTP server. Four PoE ports out of eight is the point of the entry - the nearest existing TP-Link entry, tl-sg105, is the five-port non-PoE model, and tl-sg1016pe is PoE on 8 of 16 ports.

label: TP-Link TL-SG1008MP
description: TP-Link TL-SG1008MP - eight-port unmanaged gigabit desktop/rackmount switch with PoE+ on all eight ports: 8x 10/100/1000 RJ45, 802.3af/at at up to 30 W per port against a 153 W total budget, 16 Gbps switching capacity, rack-mountable 1U, internal 100-240 V AC PSU.

poe.note: PoE+ on all eight ports, IEEE 802.3af/at, up to 30 W per port with a 153 W total budget. Eight ports at 30 W is 240 W of demand, so the budget is the binding constraint: five 30 W devices is the practical ceiling. Extend mode applies to ports 1-2 only (rate drops to 10 Mbps for runs to 250 m) and PoE auto recovery is supported.

fabric.note: Vendor switching capacity of 16 Gbps, the full-duplex aggregate of the eight gigabit ports (8 Gbps each way).

notes: TP-Link figures from the current product pages (https://www.tp-link.com/uk/business-networking/unmanaged-switch/tl-sg1008mp/ and https://www.tp-link.com/us/business-networking/unmanaged-switch/tl-sg1008mp/) and the current TL-SG1008MP(UN) datasheet. Hardware: 8x 10/100/1000 Mbps RJ45 with PoE+ on every port, 16 Gbps switching capacity, 4 K MAC table, 16 KB jumbo frames, store-and-forward, 802.1p priority, auto MDI/MDIX, 294 x 180 x 44 mm 1U metal case with rack-mount kit, internal 100-240 V AC supply, 8.77 W with no PD and 172.49 W with a 153 W PoE load, 29.91 / 588.19 BTU/h heat, operating range 0 to 50 C, LEDs for Power, PoE MAX, 1000 Mbps, Link/Act and PoE status. Unmanaged: no CLI, no HTTP server. DISCREPANCIES: (1) revision V1 of this model published a 126 W PoE budget (https://www.tp-link.com/gr/business-networking/unmanaged-switch/tl-sg1008mp/v1/) while the current revision and its datasheet publish 153 W - this entry follows the current 153 W figure, so a lab built from a V1 unit has 27 W less to give than the entry allows. (2) Cooling is unresolved: the US and UK product pages describe the box as fanless while the datasheet lists one fan, so no fan claim is made here. Neither discrepancy touches port count, port type or the PoE standard.

label: TP-Link TL-SG1005LP
description: TP-Link TL-SG1005LP - five-port unmanaged gigabit desktop switch with PoE+ on four ports and a 40 W budget: 5x 10/100/1000 RJ45, 802.3af/at at up to 30 W each on ports 1-4, 10 Gbps switching capacity, fanless, external 53.5 V DC adapter.

poe.note: PoE standard 802.3af/at, ports 1-4, up to 30 W per port against a 40 W budget. Because the budget is 40 W, one 30 W PoE+ device leaves 10 W - a second 30 W device is refused by the switch, not merely drawn beyond spec. Intelligent power management sheds lower-priority ports above 40 W. PoE auto recovery on ports 1-4; extend mode on ports 1-2 only, dropping those ports to 10 Mbps for runs up to 250 m.

fabric.note: Vendor switching capacity of 10 Gbps, the full-duplex aggregate of the five gigabit ports (5 Gbps each way).

notes: TP-Link figures from datasheet TL-SG1005LP(UN) 4.0 (https://static.tp-link.com/upload/product-overview/2026/202609/20260924/TL-SG1005LP(UN)4.0_datasheet.pdf), cross-checked against the UK product page (https://www.tp-link.com/uk/business-networking/poe-switch/tl-sg1005lp/). Hardware: 5x 10/100/1000 Mbps RJ45, auto negotiation and auto MDI/MDIX, PoE+ on ports 1-4, 10 Gbps switching capacity, 7.44 Mpps forwarding, 2 K MAC table, 1 Mbit packet buffer, store-and-forward, 802.1p/DSCP QoS, IGMP snooping, fanless metal desktop/wall case 99.8 x 98 x 25 mm fed by an external 53.5 V DC / 0.81 A adapter, 46.9 W maximum consumption, 159.46 BTU/h, MTBF 611,257 h at 25 C, operating range -5 to 40 C. Unmanaged: no CLI, no HTTP server. Jumbo frame is 9 KB in the datasheet but 16 KB on the product page - the datasheet figure is used. Against the TL-SG1005P this box trades 25 W of PoE budget (40 W against 65 W) on the same port layout, which is the difference that decides whether two PoE+ cameras fit on one unit.
